newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia asks 6 Telstra directors to quit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia asks 6 Telstra directors to quit.

text.p: The Australian government said on Friday it had asked for the resignation of six board members of government-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp.
A spokesman for Communications Minister Richard Alston said the board members were asked to resign because the government viewed them as unsuitable to guide Telstra's future growth.

"Basically, the new board members have a combination of talent and drive and have demonstrated success in the commercial market and that's what's needed to take Telstra into the 21st century," the spokesman told Reuters.
Deputy chairman Mark Burrows was among those asked to resign. The others were Bill Mansfield, John Menadue, Brian Finn, Steven Wilson and Helen Williams.
The spokesman said Fosters Brewing Group Ltd chairman John Ralph had been appointed as deputy chairman.
The other replacements were former CSIRO head John Stocker, television personality Stephen Vizard, Santos Ltd managing director Ross Adler and Anthony Clark.
David Hoare and Frank Blount would remain as chairman and chief executive respectively.
"There are significant challenges facing the board of Telstra, including preparing for open competition in the telecommunications market from July 1, 1997," Alston said in a statement.
Alston said the new board members would be formally appointed shortly.
The government has introduced a bill for the partial privatisation of Telstra and hopes to raise A$8.0 billion from the sale.
The bill faces tough opposition in parliament's Upper House, the Senate, where the government does not have a clear majority.
